newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market ends weaker despite bill mkt rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market ends weaker despite bill mkt rally.

text.p: * Telecom-led NZ share market drifts lower at close
* Bill market rally fails to fire market
* Cultus rises after report of new gas field find
Price movements at close

The New Zealand share market lost early gains by the close of an insipid day's trading on Wednesday.
A sharp rally on the bank bill market failed to spark equities and, in the light of that, brokers expect the market to continue to drift before next week's key March quarter inflation data.
The top 40 index ended 3.92 points down at 2,2220.7 after sluggish volume of $39 million.
"For the rest of the week I can't see us going anywhere different from where we have been the last couple of days," said Merrill Lynch broker Tim Koller.
"Then next week, when we get the CPI number, if that is more favourable (then) commentators will be looking at an easing later in the year and that's got to be beneficial," he said.
While the U.S. market had stabilised, investors were still wary of further fallout on Wall Street, dealers said.
The market drifted as Telecom lost morning gains to end five cents weaker at $6.50.
Cultus Petroleum, a fast-moving share during the past six months, gained 30 cents to $3.20, after it reported a new gas field in the Otway Basin.
There was interest in some banking sector stocks after the Wallace Commission report was released in Australia.
National Mutual rose 10 cents to $2.10 after the commission gave the green light to mergers for life offices and banks.
Conversely, ANZ Bank fell 35 cents to $8.75 when the commission held a ban on bank mergers amongst the big four Australians.
